findings.title: The blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive, so they can be bypassed.
findings.body: `blacklistedGuestEmails` is lowercased but `guest` is not. Submitting `Blocked@Example.com` gets past `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS`. The same exact-match comparison against `attendee.email` lets `Existing@x.com` be added as a duplicate of `existing@x.com`. Lowercase `guest` (and the attendee emails) before comparing.

findings.title: The emails are sent with the raw `guests` list instead of `uniqueGuests`.
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` uses `newGuests.includes(attendee.email)` to decide who gets the "you're scheduled" email. If the request includes an address that was already an attendee, that existing attendee is treated as new and gets a booking-confirmation email instead of the guests-added notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: The server never checks that guest emails are unique and does not limit how many can be sent.
findings.body: The uniqueness `refine` only exists in the client dialog. A direct API call with `["a@x.com","a@x.com"]` passes `uniqueGuests` (which only compares against existing attendees) and creates duplicate attendee rows, each of which gets an email. The array also has no maximum length, so any attendee can make the server send booking emails to an unlimited number of arbitrary addresses. Add a uniqueness refine and a `.max(...)` to this schema.

findings.title: The admin-or-owner check uses `&&`, so it only lets owners through.
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` requires both `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` to be true. A team admin who is not an owner is refused with FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. The variable name says either role should be enough. Use `||` here, or rely on `isTeamAdmin` alone if it already accepts owners.

findings.title: The fallback error message can never be shown, and the invalid-email warning is never cleared.
findings.body: The template string is never empty, so `message || t("unable_to_add_guests")` always uses `message`, which can read like "undefined: ...". Separately, `isInvalidEmail` is never reset after a successful add or when the user edits the emails, so the warning stays visible the next time the dialog opens. Use the fallback when `err.data?.code` is missing, and reset `isInvalidEmail` in `onSuccess` and when the emails change.

findings.title: A booking with no `userId` makes this call throw a generic 500 error.
findings.body: When `booking.userId` is null, the code looks up user id 0 and `findFirstOrThrow` throws a Prisma not-found error, so the client gets an unhandled 500 error. Check for a missing organizer first and throw a TRPCError with a clear code.
